Welcome toGas in a Water Bath

A gas expands in a 300 K water bath — how much work comes out?

How would you like to begin?

Listen to the intro

About: Work, heat and the Helmholtz function in an expansion at the bath temperature

Source

Concept
Work Wby, heat Q, entropy generated Sgen and the Helmholtz function F = U − TS for ν = 1.00 mol of ideal gas expanding from V₁ = 10.0 L to V₂ = rV₁ in a water bath at T = 300 K.
Model
The load is lowered in n equal-ratio steps, Vₖ = V₁rk/n, with pext = νRT/Vₖ on step k, or reversibly along the isotherm. The piston is damped and the gas returns to 300 K between steps; the work on a step is pext(Vₖ − Vₖ₋₁), Q is the heat taken from the bath, and T Sgen = TνR ln r − Q, with R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Serves
Relating the work delivered at the bath temperature to −ΔF, to the path taken, and to the entropy generated.
Inquiry
Five questions, each answered by running an expansion and reading the bars and the Readouts panel in the sidebar (which keeps the previous run for comparison), then a closing summary card.
Misconception
Common intuitions are carried by the answer choices and addressed only in the feedback to the choice a student makes.

Pedagogy principles applied

PrincipleHow this sim honours it
Commit, then checkEach answer is committed before its run; the work, heat and T Sgen bars start empty after every Reset piston and at each new question.
Staged revealsThe Q bar, the T Sgen bar, its shaded gap on the p–V graph and the matching readouts appear only at the questions that ask about them; all appear in free exploration. A key on the graph names each area: Wby under the orange path, −ΔF under the isotherm, T Sgen between them.
Operational quantitiesEnergies in joules on a fixed 0–5000 J axis; pressure in kPa (0–275) and volume in L (0–65) on fixed axes that never rescale.
One pictureThe piston sits directly above its volume on the p–V graph, so the motion of the piston and the path it traces read together.
Real valuesν = 1.00 mol, T = 300 K, V₁ = 10.0 L, R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹; animation timing is not physical time, and the arrow length is proportional to pext.
Controls respond liveChanging r moves the isotherm end point and the −ΔF bar at once; changing n redraws the stop marks on the cylinder.

Guided Inquiry

1 · A single step

Set the volume ratio to 4 and the number of steps to 1, and press Run. The load is lowered in a single step, straight to the final pressure. How does the work Wby done by the gas compare with −ΔF?

2 · More steps

Keep the volume ratio at 4 and run the expansion in 2, 3, 5, 10 and 20 steps in turn; the Previous run card in Readouts keeps the last result. What happens to Wby as the number of steps increases?

3 · The heat from the bath

Run any expansion and watch the bar Q for the heat taken from the bath. How does Q compare with Wby?

4 · The entropy generated

Set the volume ratio to 4 and one step, run it, and then run the reversible expansion. How does the bar T Sgen compare with the gap between −ΔF and Wby?

5 · Larger volume ratios

Set one step and compare the readout Wby/(−ΔF) at volume ratio 2 with that at volume ratio 6. What happens to the fraction?

6 · Work at the bath temperature

At a fixed temperature the work a gas delivers depends on the path, but it never exceeds −ΔF = νRT ln r, the area under the isotherm.

The heat drawn from the bath always equals the work, because U stays fixed.

The shortfall, −ΔF − Wby, is T Sgen: T times the entropy generated. Only the reversible path, with Sgen = 0, delivers all of −ΔF. Press Finish to explore freely.

Gas in a Water Bath

✦Learn this with the AI tutor

01

At a glance

One mole of gas sits in a cylinder in a 300 K water bath while a load on the piston is lowered in steps. The gas expands and does work. The sim keeps the accounts: the work delivered, the heat taken from the bath, a lost-work term T Sgen, and the Helmholtz drop −ΔF.

What you'll learn

  • What the bars Wby, Q, T Sgen and −ΔF measure.
  • How Wby depends on n and r.
  • How Wby compares with −ΔF and Q.
  • Where T Sgen comes from.
The set-up: gas, loaded piston, 300 K bath.

What's on screen

  • Orange path: pext, the pressure the load holds. Wby is the area under it, and the orange bar.
  • Grey isotherm: the gas's own pressure. −ΔF is the area under it, and the grey bar.
  • Purple gap: between path and isotherm. It is T Sgen, and the purple bar.
  • Blue bar: Q, the heat from the bath. All bars share a 0–5000 J axis.
  • Readouts: This run and Previous run.
See itRun the sim at your current settings. Watch for: the piston moving out, the orange path appearing on the p–V graph, and the bars rising.

Fixed: ν = 1.00 mol of ideal gas, T = 300 K, V1 = 10.0 L, R = 8.314 J mol−1 K−1. On step k the load holds pext = νRT/Vk, and the gas returns to 300 K between steps. Run times are not physical time.

03

At fixed temperature the work is capped by −ΔF

Put a system in contact with a reservoir at temperature T. The first law and the Clausius inequality, δQ ≤ T dS, together give −δW ≤ −dF, where F = U − TS (notes 3.17 and 3.18). Integrated over a change at constant T, the work done by the system obeys the bound below, with equality only for a reversible change. The notes' own example is a gas in a water bath, which is this sim.

Wby ≤ −ΔF = Fi − Ff
Notes (3.19).

For the ideal gas U depends only on T, so ΔU = 0 and ΔF = −TΔS = −νRT ln r. At r = 4 that gives −ΔF = 2494.2 J × ln 4 = 3458 J, the area under the isotherm from 10.0 L at 249.4 kPa to 40.0 L at 62.4 kPa.

The sim's p–V graph at r = 4: −ΔF is the area under the isotherm.
See itRun the reversible expansion at r = 4. Watch for: the orange path lying along the isotherm, and the Wby bar rising to meet the −ΔF bar.
04

One step stops short of the isotherm

In a single step the load drops straight to the final pressure pext = νRT/V2 and stays there. At r = 4 that is 62.4 kPa, far below the 249.4 kPa the gas starts at, so for most of the stroke the gas pushes against much less than its own pressure. The work is the rectangle under the orange line.

Wby = pext(V2 − V1) = νRT(1 − 1/r)

At r = 4 this is 62.4 kPa × 30.0 L = 1871 J, which is 54.1% of the 3458 J limit. The gap between the rectangle and the isotherm, 1587 J, is work the expansion could have delivered and did not.

One step at r = 4, drawn from the sim's model.
See itRun one step at r = 4. Watch for: the orange path dropping to 62.4 kPa at once and running flat to 40.0 L, with the Wby bar well below the −ΔF bar.
05

More steps lift the staircase towards the isotherm

Lower the load in n steps of equal volume ratio, so the gas ends step k at Vk = V1rk/n, and on that step let pext = νRT/Vk, the pressure that would hold the gas at Vk. Each step adds a rectangle, and the staircase hugs the isotherm from below.

Wby = ∑ pext(Vk − Vk−1) = nνRT(1 − r−1/n)

At r = 4 the sum gives 1871, 2494, 2769, 3020, 3229 and 3341 J for n = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 and 20. Each doubling of n adds less: 623 J from 1 to 2 steps, 112 J from 10 to 20. Every sum stays below νRT ln r. Only the reversible run, the n → ∞ limit, reaches it.

Wby at r = 4 for each setting of n.
See itThe sim runs n = 1, 5 and 20 in turn at r = 4. Watch for: the staircase gaining steps, and Wby in the Previous run card creeping up towards the −ΔF bar.
06

The heat equals the work; the gap is T Sgen

The gas returns to 300 K between steps, and an ideal gas's U depends only on T, so ΔU = 0 over the run. The first law then gives Q = Wby: every joule of work arrives as heat from the bath, and the Q bar always matches the Wby bar. Meanwhile the gas's entropy rises by νR ln r and the bath's falls by Q/T, so the entropy generated is Sgen = νR ln r − Q/T.

T Sgen = νRT ln r − Q = −ΔF − Wby

T Sgen is the purple gap on the p–V graph. By notes (2.55) it is the work that can no longer be obtained. It cannot be negative, which is the bound Wby ≤ −ΔF again, and it is zero only for the reversible run.

r = 4Wby (J)Q (J)T Sgen (J)−ΔF (J)

See itThe sim runs one step, then the reversible run, at r = 4. Watch for: the Q bar matching the Wby bar in both runs, and the purple T Sgen bar shrinking to nothing in the second.
07

A larger ratio collects a smaller share

For one step, Wby = νRT(1 − 1/r) stays below νRT = 2494 J however large r gets, while −ΔF = νRT ln r keeps growing. So the share collected falls with r.

Wby/(−ΔF) = (1 − 1/r) / ln r   for n = 1

The share is 72.1% at r = 2, 54.1% at r = 4 and 46.5% at r = 6. The final pressure νRT/V2 falls as r grows, from 124.7 to 62.4 to 41.6 kPa, so the gas pushes against a lower and lower pressure. More steps recover most of the loss: at r = 6, twenty steps collect 95.7%.

Wby/(−ΔF) against r, from the sim's model.
See itThe sim runs one step at r = 2, then at r = 6. Watch for: the Previous run card holding the r = 2 result, and the new fraction landing lower.
08

Where it matters

  • Isothermal strokes of an engine. The notes' Carnot cycle has isothermal legs. Reaching −ΔF takes a reversible stroke, which is a limit that no finite machine reaches, so every real stroke loses T Sgen.
  • Chemical cells. The same argument at constant T and p bounds the non-expansion work by the Gibbs function, δW′ ≥ dG (notes 3.20), which is what limits the electrical work of a cell.
  • Lost work. Notes (2.55): the work that can no longer be obtained is the entropy generated times the temperature of the coldest body available, here the bath.
Go deeper: why Q = Wby even in the one-step run

During a fast step the gas does not stay at 300 K. The sim's piston is damped and it lets the gas return to 300 K between steps, so the heat flows in while the piston is at rest, from the 300 K bath into the cooler gas, until both are at one temperature again. Over the whole run U is back where it started, so the bath supplies exactly the work delivered: 1871 J in the one-step run, not 3458 J.

09

Summary

In one line. The sim lowers a load on a gas in a 300 K bath in n steps at volume ratio r, and shows Wby, Q, T Sgen and −ΔF as areas, bars and readouts.

Key points

  • At fixed T, Wby ≤ −ΔF = νRT ln r, with equality only for the reversible run.
  • Wby rises with n and falls short of −ΔF by T Sgen.
  • Q = Wby in every run, since ΔU = 0.

Common mix-ups

  • “The work equals −ΔF however you lower the load.” One step at r = 4 gives 1871 J. Only the reversible path reaches 3458 J.
  • “More steps can overshoot the isotherm.” The sums for n = 1 to 20 climb to 3341 J and stay under 3458 J.
  • “The heat from the bath is −ΔF.” Q = Wby: one step takes 1871 J from the bath, not 3458 J.

Things to try on your own

  • At r = 6, compare the share Wby/(−ΔF) for 1 and 20 steps.
  • Run rev at each r and check that Wby equals −ΔF.
  • For several n, check that Q equals Wby.
